source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure routing distribution, expert capacity overflow, all-to-all time, token dropping/padding, placement, batch composition, and compare routing/capacity policies.
corrected_answer: Assume the checkpoint, expert count, top-k, precision, kernels, runtime version, hardware/topology, autoscaling policy, offered load, concurrency, and request-length mix are fixed; report milliseconds, token counts, rates, and confidence intervals, separating measured facts from estimates. Falsifiable hypothesis for variant 104: router assignment skew and capacity pressure are the dominant causes of tail latency; under identical offered load, a preregistered routing/load-balancing or capacity-factor treatment will reduce maximum per-expert load, overflow, token drops/padding, and p99 while preserving quality, goodput, SLO attainment, and acceptable cost. Use matched replicas and fixed-seed randomized requests, one policy change at a time, tuning only on a disjoint set, then evaluate held-out replay and canary at unchanged load. Measure router scores/entropy and assignment distribution; per-expert token counts, capacity, overflow, drops, padding, utilization; queue, expert compute, dispatch/combine, all-to-all and link time; placement/topology; batch and sequence composition; throughput, p50/p95/p99, quality, goodput, SLOs, errors, retries, memory, and cost. Stratify by expert, sequence length, tenant, concurrency, and load. Confounders include queueing, batching, warmup, autoscaling, correlated traffic, kernel/precision effects, communication contention, and quality-sensitive routing. The treatment is not accepted if quality or severe-error rate worsens, SLO/goodput or cost breaches the preregistered bound, or attribution is unclear. Canary and rollback on sustained p99/SLO regression, overflow/drops, error rate, memory pressure, or quality guardrail breach; restore the last known-good policy and retain telemetry. Do not infer causality from aggregate latency alone.
